edition: Migne PG 59 (homiliae 1-88); the DCO clean text is the TLG digitization keyed to PG 59 columns.
license: Scans: public domain. Clean DCO MGR text: NOT open - header states it is Thesaurus Linguae Graecae, copyright UC Irvine, posted to DCO by special 2008 permission only (user already excludes TLG).
completeness: Clean DCO/TLG text is ~100% (full homilies 1-88, verified polytonic with [59.xx] column markers and TLG serial '2062 153') but unusable under open license. Open (PD) material is 100% as scans only.
notes: Decisive caveat: DCO's MGR PDF is genuinely clean, fully-accented polytonic running text keyed to PG columns - BUT it carries the TLG/UC-Irvine copyright, so it fails the open-license bar. No open clean-text alternative found. Classified 'scan' because the only openly-licensed form is the PD Migne page-images, which need OCR.

format: Open option: PD page-image scan (PG 55, GM ~174 MB). A clean extractable polytonic-text PDF exists at DCO (MGR file) but is license-encumbered.
edition: Migne PG 55; DCO clean text is the TLG digitization keyed to PG 55 columns.
license: Scans: public domain. Clean DCO MGR text: NOT open - TLG/UC-Irvine copyright (same restriction as In Joannem).
completeness: Clean DCO/TLG text verified (TLG serial '2062 143', full polytonic with [55.xx] markers) and covers the surviving Psalm commentary (selected psalms; the work was never a complete 1-150 set, starts ~Psalm 4); ~100% of what survives, but license-encumbered. Open (PD) form is scan-only.
notes: Same TLG-copyright caveat as In Joannem: clean text is real and high quality but not openly licensed. The genuine Chrysostom Psalm commentary in PG 55 is intrinsically partial (selected psalms only), so 'completeness' is relative to the surviving work, not all 150 psalms. Open route is OCR of the PD PG 55 scan.

work: Eusebius of Caesarea, Commentaria in Psalmos (Commentary on the Psalms)
format: TEI P5 XML, native digital transcription (not OCR). Three Greek files: pta0003.pta020.pta-grcBibex1/2/3.xml (~1.53 + 3.92 + 2.53 MB). Raw XML downloadable from the GitHub 'public' branch; JS web reader at pta.bbaw.de.
edition: New BBAW critical digital edition via the Patristic Text Archive (2020): Villani (Ps 1-50), Bandt & Coullet (Ps 51-100, = GCS.NF 30), Risch (Ps 101-150). NOT the Migne PG 23-24 text.
license: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0), stated in each file's teiHeader.
completeness: ~100% of the work - all 150 psalms across 3 volumes present as Greek TEI.
notes: Verified real Greek body text in raw XML (e.g. 'O men lg psalmos eiretai to Dauid...'). Caveat: this is a DIFFERENT edition from Migne PG 23-24 - the modern critical text reconstructs Ps 1-50 and 101-150 from catena fragments (only Ps 51-100 transmitted intact), so coverage/lemmatization differs from Migne. CC BY-SA is copyleft (ShareAlike), not NC - usable but viral. The dilemma/corpus project already ingests PTA, so this work may already be partly covered; confirm pta0003.pta020 is in the local pta_data pull. First1KGreek does NOT have tlg2018.034 (its tlg2018 dir stops at tlg023). DCO has only an image-PDF Migne scan.

format: Image-PDF page scans only (DCO ~7.4 MB Google-Books reproduction of Migne PG 110; archive.org/HathiTrust scans of de Boor Teubner). Any embedded text layer is noisy Google/IA OCR, not clean transcription.
edition: Migne PG 110 (Chronicon breve, Muralt recension) for the DCO scan; archive.org/HathiTrust carry de Boor's 1904 Teubner edition (the longer Chronicon, not the PG breve).
completeness: 0% clean digital text. Scans only - would require OCR.
notes: No clean Greek running text found anywhere open: NOT in First1KGreek (data/tlg3043 -> 404), NOT in PTA, NOT on Perseus/Scaife or ToposText. Despite the 'MGR' label, the DCO file for this Byzantine chronicle is an image scan (its catalog uses MGR loosely; unlike the Chrysostom MGR files it is not a TLG transcription). Only the licensed TLG has clean digital Georgius Monachus text (excluded). Edition split: PG 110 = Chronicon breve; de Boor = the longer Chronicon (overlapping, not identical). The project's calfa-co PG OCR already covers PG 110 as noisy OCR.
